telnet_ipv4_enabled.description: Enable the Telnet service on IPv4 (TCP port 23)

telnet_ipv6_enabled.description: Enable the Telnet service on IPv6 (TCP port 23); enable only if the network stack requires it

run_user.description: Unix user that in.telnetd runs as; root is required for PAM-based login

use_tcp_wrappers.description: Route every connection through tcpd to enforce host-based ACLs defined in /etc/hosts.allow and /etc/hosts.deny

tcpd_path.description: Absolute path to the tcpd binary; relevant only when use_tcp_wrappers is true

telnetd_path.description: Absolute path to the in.telnetd binary installed by inetutils-telnetd

telnetd_options.description: Extra flags passed to in.telnetd, e.g. ["-a","none"] to disable Telnet auth negotiation or ["-L","/bin/login"] to specify the login program

extra_services.description: Additional inetd service entries appended after the telnet blocks; each entry becomes one line in inetd.conf

name.description: Service name from /etc/services or a numeric port number

socket_type.description: Socket type: stream, dgram, raw, rdm, or seqpacket

proto.description: Transport protocol: tcp, udp, tcp6, udp6, or an RPC specification

wait.description: wait or nowait; optionally append .max-connections, e.g. nowait.10

user.description: Unix user (optionally .group) the server program runs as

server_path.description: Absolute path to the server executable

args.description: Space-separated arguments passed to the server executable; leave empty if none

comment.description: One-line description rendered as a comment above this service entry
